QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_6

question.text: Mr. Arjun Kulkarni, CFO of Narmada Cat II AIF (a SEBI-registered trust), asks which India tax form is used to pass through income details to unit-holders so they can report their share in their personal returns under the Section 115UB pass-through regime:

answer.text: Form 64C — statement of income distributed to unit-holders

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 115UB and Rule 12CB, Cat I/II AIFs issue Form 64C to unit-holders showing the nature and amount of income passed through. The fund also files Form 64D with the tax authorities consolidating the allocation. This is the Indian equivalent of a US LP's K-1. The Trap: 15G is a TDS waiver form for resident individuals. 26AS is the IT department's own credit summary. 3CEB applies to transfer-pricing-reportable international transactions — irrelevant to AIF pass-through. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B mention 64C conceptually. XIX-C expects the Manager to know 64C vs 64D distinction and filing deadlines. XXIV (AML) does not test this. Manager's Pro-Tip: Deliver 64C to LPs by 30-Jun each year — delays push domestic LPs into filing-deadline panic and wreck GP-LP goodwill. Automate extraction from the fund accounting system; don't rely on the auditor's post-sign-off schedule.
